item.title: Lawyers in the Library: Employment & Civil Law — Thu Oct 22, 12:00 PM — Central Santa Rosa Library
item.description: Local volunteer attorneys offer free legal information and referral for matters of civil and employment law only. These lawyer consultations will last up to 20 minutes. Sign-ups are first come, first served in person and begin at 11:30 am. \(30 minutes before the program begins\) The attorneys are volunteers and provide only legal information. They do not provide specific legal advice and should not be considered as personal lawyers for any reason. You will be required to sign a waiver before speaking to an attorney that states that no attorney-client relationship is being created with this free service. Spanish language consultations are available via translator. Participants may bring support persons, family members or other affiliated persons to meet with the attorney together. For deaf and hard of hearing participants, the Sonoma County Bar Association will make arrangements for ASL interpretation with at least two days' advance notice. Please contact Reception@SonomaCountyBar.org

item.title: Samba no Pé — Thu Oct 22, 6:30 PM — 4140 Redwood Highway #8 • San Rafael
item.description:
Get ready to feel the rhythm and energy of Rio de Janeiro! **Samba no Pé** (Samba in the Foot) is the captivating solo style of samba danced in the streets and at Carnival, known for its rapid, intricate footwork and infectious hip movements.
**You will learn**
The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.
Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.
Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.
Rhythm & Musicality: You will learn how to connect your movement directly to the irresistible beat of the bateria (the samba drum section).

item.description:

Great for first timers!

item.description:
Discover the Moringa tree in this class designed by Moringa University. Whether you are a gardening enthusiast, a wellness advocate, or passionate about sustainable living, this class will deepen your connection to regenerative agriculture and holistic health.
What You Will Learn:
The essentials of planting, nurturing, and harvesting Moringa.
Explore the health benefits and culinary uses of this nutrient-dense plant.
Honor the global history and traditional medicinal roots of the Moringa tree.

item.title: The Art of Broom Making — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM — Gather Sebastopol
item.description:
Join us for a hands-on workshop where tradition meets artistry. Alissa Kaplan, maker and founder of Zizland Atelier, will guide you through the craft of broom making as you create your own Wrapped Hawk Tail Whisk—a beautiful and functional hand broom with deep roots in American folk tradition.
In this 3-hour class, you’ll learn:
• A brief history and uses of hand brooms
• Traditional Shaker/Appalachian binding and wrapping techniques
• How to select and prepare broomcorn for a whisk
• Step-by-step guidance to craft your own wrapped Hawk Tail Whisk to take home
Whether you’re drawn to heritage crafts, seasonal rituals, or simply love working with your hands, this workshop offers a meaningful way to connect with timeless skills and leave with something useful and beautiful.
Some hand strength is required. Material and tools will be supplied.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Fresh Cheesemaking with Botanical Flavors — Sat Oct 24, 4:00 PM — Gather Sebastopol
item.description:
Fresh cheese is one of the most approachable and rewarding things to make at home. In Sonoma County’s rich dairy landscape, these simple cheeses have long been a staple—equally at home in everyday meals and on a shared table.
In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn how to make fresh cheeses from cow and goat milk, while exploring how herbs, flowers, and citrus can shape flavor in simple, elegant ways. We’ll cover the essential techniques behind fresh cheesemaking so you can confidently recreate them in your own kitchen.
In this workshop you’ll:
• Learn the fundamentals of fresh cheesemaking using cow and goat milk
• Understand key concepts in cheesemaking, including acidity, texture, and food safety
• Make goat milk chèvre with edible flowers and with rosemary and honey
• Prepare fresh ricotta with Meyer lemon
• Explore how to incorporate herbs, flowers, and other botanicals into your cheeses

Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. item.title: Poet Jeremy Raikes’s book signing — Sun Oct 25, 4:00 PM — Wonderland Pizzeria
item.description:
Poet Jeremy Raikes (well known to many in Sonoma County as the Chair Repair Guy!) will celebrate his 90th birthday and the publication of his poetry collection, *Delicious Suspicions*, with a book signing and birthday gathering on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. at Wonderland Pizzeria, 20391 Highway 116 in Monte Rio.
Raised on a cattle ranch in Argentina by expat British parents, in the 1960's Jeremy was an advertising writer at J Walter Thompson (then the largest advertising agency in the world) and later became creative director of their Mexico City office. While at Thompson, Jeremy collaborated with Charles Schultz on a series of animated Peanuts ads for the Ford Motor Company.
The occasion offers readers a chance to meet Jeremy, purchase a signed copy of his book and celebrate a writer whose work approaches life with humor, tenderness and an enduring sense of wonder.
